mainTopic: Laws of orphans' property and their stewards (sales, removal, and oaths), and a new משנה on causing hidden damage to another's food or wine.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a reason from the previous page: if money alone finalized a sale, a paid seller could just say 'your wheat burned in the attic.' The גמרא then discusses buyers who paid orphans for produce, and רב שישא בריה דרב אידי explains why a special rule for orphans would actually hurt them. רב אשי reports a sale of an orphan's land without a public announcement, which is allowed for head tax, food, and burial. A story follows about עמרם צבעא, a steward whom the relatives accused before רב נחמן. The הלכה is that a steward is removed only if witnesses show he is causing loss. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's dispute about which steward must swear. The first opinion says the steward appointed by the father, אבא שאול says the one appointed by בית דין, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says both. A new משנה then teaches about one who makes another's food טמא, mixes in תרומה, or pours wine to an idol. רב and שמואל argue about what 'pouring' means, and רב's full reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The danger: 'Your wheat burned in the attic'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a reason from the previous discussion. If a seller has already been paid and the produce counts as the buyers', he will not bother saving it from a fire. He will just say 'your wheat burned.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the sellers will come and say to them: 'Your wheat was burned in the upper story.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a reason that began earlier. It explains the danger of letting money alone finalize a purchase of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the produce already belongs to the buyer but still sits in the seller's house, the seller has no reason to protect it. If a fire breaks out, he will not try to save it, and he will simply report that it burned. This is why money alone should not finalize the sale.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new case. It is the end of a reason given just before this point.

phrases.english: For they will come to say to them:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the sellers who were already paid, and 'them' are the buyers.

phrases.english: Your wheat was burned in the upper story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a reason from the material just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reasoning: the risk that a paid seller will neglect the goods.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money alone does not finalize the purchase, so that the seller stays responsible for the produce.

steps.title: Buyers paid orphans for produce and the price went up
steps.stepSummary: Buyers paid the orphans money for produce but did not yet pull it into their possession. If the price rose, the orphans may back out, because an ordinary party should not be stronger than הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they gave money to the orphans for produce and the price went up, the power of an ordinary person should not be greater than that of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new case: buyers paid orphans for produce that was not yet handed over, and then the price rose. The ruling is that the orphans may back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the orphans are the sellers. Since no pulling (משיכה) took place, the sale is not final. The גמרא uses the rule that an ordinary person (הדיוט) cannot have more power than הקדש, so the orphans are not stuck with the old, lower price.

phrases.english: If they gave money to the orphans for produce;
phrases.notes: The buyers paid, but they did not yet pull the produce into their possession.

phrases.english: if it went up in price –

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא כֹּחַ הֶדְיוֹט חָמוּר מֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: the power of an ordinary person should not be stronger than that of the Temple treasury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new case where orphans are the sellers who received money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the price rose and no pulling took place, the orphans may back out of the sale.

steps.title: Price went down: the students link it to רב חנילאי בר אידי
steps.stepSummary: If the price fell, the students assumed the case depends on רב חנילאי בר אידי's view. In that view, the money alone finalizes a sale involving orphans, so the orphans keep the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it went down in price, they understood from this that it is the view of רב חנילאי בר אידי.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side of the case: the price fell and the orphans want to keep the sale. The students assume this matches רב חנילאי בר אידי's view, which sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנילאי בר אידי held that for orphans, paying money finalizes the sale. If so, the buyers are locked in at the old higher price, which helps the orphans. This is only the students' assumption, and the next step questions it.

phrases.english: If it went down in price –
they understood from this,
that this is the ruling of רב חנילאי בר אידי;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Covers the opposite outcome (price drop) of the case in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students assume that when the price fell, the money alone binds the buyers, following רב חנילאי בר אידי.

steps.title: רב שישא: such a rule would hurt the orphans
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי rejects the students' assumption. If money alone finalized the orphans' sales, nobody would pay them in advance, and they could not get money when they needed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said to them: This is bad for them. Sometimes they need money, and no one will give it to them until they hand over the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא pushes back on the students. He argues that a special rule binding buyers by money alone would actually harm the orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If buyers knew that their payment locks them in even when prices drop, they would refuse to pay the orphans in advance. Then the orphans could not raise quick money when they need it. So it is better for orphans to follow the normal rules of selling.
steps.whatToRemember: A special rule meant to protect orphans should not be applied if it ends up hurting them in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said to them:
This is bad for them –
for sometimes they need money,
and there will be no one who gives it to them
until they give them the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי הָא רָעָה הוּא לְדִידְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the students' assumption in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that orphans' sales should be finalized by money alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such a rule would stop buyers from paying the orphans in advance, which harms the orphans.

steps.title: רב אשי signed a sale made without an announcement
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he and רב כהנא signed a deed for the mother of זעירא the orphan. She sold land to pay the head tax without a public announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I and רב כהנא signed a deed for the mother of זעירא the orphan, who sold land for the head tax without an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אשי tells of a real case where an orphan's land was sold without the usual public announcement, and he approved it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an orphan's property is announced before a sale, so that it gets the best price. Here the mother, acting as guardian, skipped the announcement because the head tax had to be paid. The next step gives the source that allows this.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I and Rav Kahana signed
on a deed of the mother of Ze'eira the orphan,
who sold land for the head tax
without an announcement;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אֲנָא וְרַב כָּהֲנָא חָתְמִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic about selling orphans' land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan's land sold to pay the head tax may be sold without a public announcement.

steps.title: The source: the rule of the נהרדעי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's case is based on the rule of the נהרדעי. Orphans' property may be sold without an announcement to pay the head tax, to provide food, or to pay for burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the נהרדעי said: For the head tax, for food, and for burial, we sell without an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source behind רב אשי's case. The scholars of נהרדעא allowed skipping the announcement for three urgent needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An announcement takes time. For the head tax, food, and burial, the money is needed right away, so waiting would cause harm. In these cases the urgent need outweighs getting the highest price.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally an orphan's property is announced before it is sold. For head tax, food, and burial, it may be sold without an announcement, because the money is needed right away.

phrases.english: For the scholars of Neharde'a said:
For the head tax, for food, and for burial –
we sell without an announcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the legal basis for רב אשי's case in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the sale by זעירא's mother without an announcement was valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the נהרדעי allowing sales without an announcement for head tax, food, and burial.

steps.title: Relatives complain that the steward dresses from the orphans' money
steps.stepSummary: עמרם צבעא was a steward for orphans. Relatives came to רב נחמן and complained that he dresses himself with the orphans' money.
steps.simpleTranslation: עמרם צבעא (the dyer) was a steward for orphans. Relatives came to רב נחמן and said: He dresses himself from the orphans' money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about a steward, עמרם צבעא. The orphans' relatives bring their first complaint against him to רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The relatives think his fancy clothes prove he is taking the orphans' money. This is the first of three complaints, and רב נחמן will answer each one in turn.

keyTerms.meaning: A steward or guardian who manages orphans' property

phrases.english: Amram the dyer
was a steward for orphans.
Relatives came before Rav Nachman,
they said to him:
He dresses and covers himself from the orphans!
phrases.notes: They mean he buys his clothing with the orphans' money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about the orphans' steward, moving on from selling orphans' property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fancy clothing suggests he is spending the orphans' money on himself.

steps.title: Nice clothes help him manage the property
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he may dress well so that people will listen to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: He does it so that his words will be listened to.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends the steward against the first complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A well-dressed manager gets more respect when he deals with people about the orphans' property. So the clothes may actually help the orphans and are not proof of stealing.

keyTerms.meaning: His words will be heard (people will listen to him)

phrases.english: He said to them:
So that his words will be heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first complaint.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His fancy clothes prove he is stealing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clothes may serve the orphans' interests.

steps.title: He eats and drinks well but is not rich
steps.stepSummary: The relatives complain again: he eats and drinks lavishly, and he is not known to be wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He eats and drinks from their money, and he is not a wealthy man!
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives bring a second, stronger complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing could be explained as helping the job, but food and drink only benefit him. Since he has no known wealth, they suggest the money must be coming from the orphans.

phrases.english: He eats and drinks from theirs,
and he is not wealthy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new complaint after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's defense of the steward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rich food does not help manage the property, and he has no money of his own.

steps.title: Maybe he found something valuable
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that perhaps he found a lost item and is living off that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he found a lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן again defends the steward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spending more than people expect does not prove he took from the orphans. He may have gained money in some other way, such as finding a lost object.

phrases.english: Say that he found a lost item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second complaint.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His lifestyle must be paid for by the orphans.
steps.terutzMaskana: His money could come from another source.

steps.title: But he is causing the orphans loss
steps.stepSummary: The relatives make their strongest claim: he is actually damaging the orphans' property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is causing a loss!
steps.whatsHappening: The relatives move from suspicion to a direct charge that he is losing the orphans' money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the complaints were only suspicions about where his money came from. Now they claim actual harm to the orphans' property, which is a much more serious charge.

phrases.english: But he is causing a loss!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third and stronger complaint.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A steward who loses the orphans' property should not stay in charge.

steps.title: Bring witnesses and he will be removed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says: bring witnesses that he causes loss and I will remove him, following רב הונא in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Bring me witnesses that he is causing loss, and I will remove him. As our colleague רב הונא said in the name of רב: A steward who causes loss is removed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן agrees that causing loss is grounds for removal, but he demands proof through witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suspicions are not enough, but real loss proven by עדים is. He backs this up with a rule from רב הונא in the name of רב that a steward who causes loss is removed.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Bring me witnesses that he causes loss,
and I will remove him;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא חַבְרִין מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Huna our colleague said in the name of Rav:
A steward who causes loss,
we remove him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the third complaint by accepting it in principle but requiring proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the principle and requires evidence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The relatives' claim alone should be enough to remove him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Removal requires witnesses that he actually causes loss.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical standard: a steward is not removed because of suspicion, only because of proven loss.

steps.title: The rule about removing a steward is a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב's ruling was part of a מחלוקת: רב removes a steward who causes loss, and the school of רבי שילא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: A steward who causes loss — רב הונא said in the name of רב: we remove him. The school of רבי שילא said: we do not remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the full source of רב הונא's rule and reveals that others disagreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן quoted only one side. The full statement shows that the school of רבי שילא holds that even a steward who causes loss stays in his job, so the גמרא will need to decide.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated (introduces an amoraic statement or dispute)

phrases.english: As it was stated:
A steward who causes loss,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מְסַלְּקִינַן לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav: we remove him;
the school of Rabbi Sheila say:
we do not remove him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full source behind רב נחמן's quote.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule in the name of רב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The recorded dispute between רב and the school of רבי שילא

steps.title: Final ruling: we remove him
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב: a steward who causes loss is removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: we remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute in favor of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms רב נחמן's position in the story. Once witnesses show loss, בית דין takes the steward out of his job.
steps.whatToRemember: A steward is not removed because of suspicions about his lifestyle. But if witnesses show he is causing the orphans loss, the הלכה is that he is removed.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: we remove him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute brought in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A steward proven to cause loss is removed.

steps.title: Why does a steward appointed by the father swear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a steward appointed by the orphans' father must swear, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: A steward whom the orphans' father appointed must swear. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks for the reason behind the oath rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires this steward to take an oath that he took nothing when he hands back the property. The question is why we put that burden on him.

phrases.english: A steward whom the orphans' father appointed —
must swear:
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס שֶׁמִּינָּהוּ אֲבִי יְתוֹמִים – יִשָּׁבַע: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story back to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a father-appointed steward must swear.

steps.title: He benefited from the father, so an oath will not scare him off
steps.stepSummary: He must have gotten some benefit from the father, or he would not have agreed. So an oath will not stop him from taking the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not have some benefit from him, he would not have become a steward. And he will not refuse the job because of an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the father-appointed steward swears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he had a personal reason to take the job, such as benefit from the father, we can require an oath without worrying that he will refuse. Because the oath does not discourage stewards, there is no reason to exempt him.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: If he did not have benefit from him —
phrases.notes: "From him" means from the orphans' father.

phrases.english: he would not have become a steward;
and because of an oath
he will not come to hold back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He benefited from the father, so the oath will not stop him from serving.

steps.title: A steward appointed by בית דין does not swear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a steward appointed by בית דין does not swear. He is only doing the court a favor, and an oath would make people refuse the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: If בית דין appointed him, he does not swear. He is just doing a favor for the court, and if you put an oath on him, he will refuse to serve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה and explains it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the father's steward, this one gets no benefit. He serves only as a favor to בית דין, so adding an oath would push people to turn down the job, and then the orphans would lose out.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely a favor, just a small thing

steps.whatToRemember: The oath depends on motivation. A steward appointed by the father had some benefit and will serve anyway, so he swears. A steward appointed by בית דין serves as a favor, so we do not make him swear, or nobody would take the job.

phrases.english: If the court appointed him —
he does not swear:
it is merely a favor
that he does for the court;
and if you place an oath on him,
he will come to hold back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 16 by explaining the other half of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court-appointed steward does not swear, so that people will not refuse to serve.

steps.title: אבא שאול reverses the rule
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says the rulings of the משנה are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: It is the other way around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, where אבא שאול disagrees with the first opinion. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said a father-appointed steward swears and a court-appointed steward does not. אבא שאול flips both cases: the court-appointed steward swears, and the father-appointed one does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues on the first opinion of the משנה
The matters are reversed, meaning it is the other way around

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
The matters are reversed:
phrases.notes: He means the court-appointed steward swears, and the one the father appointed does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to the משנה's first opinion explained in steps 15-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court-appointed steward swears, and a father-appointed steward does not.

steps.title: Why does a court-appointed steward swear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for אבא שאול's reason that a court-appointed steward must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that if the court appointed him, he swears?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why, according to אבא שאול, a steward appointed by בית דין must take an oath. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason a court-appointed steward did not swear was that he is only doing a favor. So the גמרא needs to explain what makes אבא שאול see the court case differently.

phrases.english: What is the reason
if the court appointed him, he swears?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא מִינּוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין יִשָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind אבא שאול's ruling in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic for requiring an oath from a court-appointed steward.

steps.title: He gains a good reputation, so an oath won't stop him
steps.stepSummary: Being chosen by the court makes him known as trustworthy, so he will still take the job even with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the benefit he gets, that word goes out about him that he is a trustworthy man, since the court relies on him, he will not refuse the job because of an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a court-appointed steward gains a good reputation. Since that benefit is worth something to him, requiring an oath will not scare him away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the same as before: if he gains something, an oath will not make him refuse. The only difference is what counts as the gain. For אבא שאול, the gain is the public honor of being trusted by בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A voice; here, public word or reputation

phrases.english: Because of that benefit
that word goes out about him
that he is a trustworthy man
since the court relies on him
he will not come to refuse because of an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהַהִיא הֲנָאָה דְּקָא נָפֵיק עֲלֵיהּ קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19, using the same reasoning as step 16 but applied to the court case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court appointment gives him a reputation as trustworthy. That benefit keeps him from refusing even if he must swear.

steps.title: Why a father-appointed steward does not swear
steps.stepSummary: A father-appointed steward is only doing a friendly favor, so an oath would make people refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the orphans' father appointed him, he does not swear. It is just a favor that people do for each other, and if you put an oath on him, he will refuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining אבא שאול by giving the other half of his view: a steward appointed by the father does not swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the roles are flipped from steps 16-17. For אבא שאול, the father's steward is the one who gains nothing, since he is just helping a friend, so an oath would scare him off. The orphans would then lose out.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely a small matter, just a favor

phrases.english: If the orphans' father appointed him, he does not swear
it is merely a favor
that people do for each other,
and if you place an oath on him,
he will come to refuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of אבא שאול, mirroring step 17 in reverse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father-appointed steward is only doing a favor, so he does not swear, so that people will not refuse the job.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions use one test: does the steward gain something? If he gains something, he swears. If he is only doing a favor, he does not. They disagree only about who gains: the father's steward, who gains from the father, or the court's steward, who gains a good reputation.

steps.title: שמואל rules like אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a ruling from שמואל that the halacha follows אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ruling, in practice the court-appointed steward swears and the father-appointed steward does not.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on שמואל's ruling

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Ami said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the מחלוקת explained in steps 18-21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to שמואל, the halacha follows אבא שאול: a court-appointed steward swears, and a father-appointed steward does not.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: both stewards swear
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that both kinds of steward swear, and the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says both this one and that one swear, and the הלכה follows his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a third opinion: every steward swears, whoever appointed him. The ברייתא adds that the הלכה follows this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new opinion that requires an oath in both cases. It comes with its own ruling, which differs from שמואל's ruling in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
This one and that one, meaning both
A תנא who holds that both stewards swear

steps.confusionAlert: There are now two rulings: שמואל rules like אבא שאול, and the ברייתא rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The גמרא records both here without deciding between them, so do not assume one cancels the other.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Both this one and that one swear,
and the halacha is like his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: זֶה וָזֶה יִשָּׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion, with its own ruling, alongside the משנה's two opinions and שמואל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every steward swears, whether the father or the court appointed him, and the halacha follows this view.

steps.title: A teaching: the father's steward swears because he is paid
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא teaches a ברייתא saying a father-appointed steward swears because he receives payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל taught before רבי אבהו: A steward appointed by the orphans' father swears, because he receives payment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא recites a ברייתא to רבי אבהו that explains why the father's steward swears. This sets up רבי אבהו's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches the first opinion of the משנה, but its wording says the steward is actually paid. The next step questions that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: רב תחליפא from the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rav Taḥalifa from the West taught
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Abbahu:
A steward appointed by the orphans' father swears,
because he receives payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first opinion of the משנה (steps 15-16) with a ברייתא giving a reason for the father-appointed steward's oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father-appointed steward swears because he is a נושא שכר.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: How do you know he was paid?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו challenges the wording: nobody actually measured any payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said to him: Did you bring a קב and measure it out for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו attacks the wording 'he receives payment.' He asks, sharply, whether anyone actually measured out wages to this steward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steward was never actually paid any set wage. We only guess that he got some benefit from the father. So calling him a real 'paid' steward goes too far.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a unit for measuring dry goods

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did you bring a kav and measure it out for him?
phrases.notes: He means: did you actually see someone pay him? Nobody did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'מפני שהוא נושא שכר' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The steward was never actually paid, so he cannot be called a real נושא שכר.

steps.title: Correct the wording: he is like someone who is paid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו fixes the text to say the steward is 'like' one who receives payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: because he is like one who receives payment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו fixes the wording of the ברייתא by adding one letter, the כ of 'like.' The steward is not paid, but he is treated as if he were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the reasoning of step 16: he must have gotten some benefit from the father. That makes him similar to a paid worker, enough to require an oath, even though no wages were given.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; a formula for correcting the wording of a text

steps.whyThisMatters: One small letter, כ, changes the claim from 'he was paid' to 'he is treated as paid.' It shows that the oath rests on the assumed benefit, not on actual wages.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
because he is like one who receives payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּנוֹשֵׂא שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 25 by correcting the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the steward is literally a paid worker.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is only 'like' a paid worker, because of the benefit he presumably got from the father, and that is enough to require an oath.
steps.whatToRemember: The father-appointed steward (according to the first opinion) swears not because he earns wages, but because he is כנושא שכר: he is treated like a paid worker because of the benefit he presumably got from the father.

steps.title: The משנה: Ruining food or wine in ways you cannot see
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that one who makes another person's food טמא, mixes תרומה into it, or pours his wine for עבודה זרה is exempt if it was an accident and must pay if it was on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who makes another person's food impure, or mixes תרומה into his produce, or pours his wine to an idol: if he did it by accident, he is exempt; if he did it on purpose, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lists three ways to cause someone a money loss without visibly touching the item, and sets the rule for paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all three cases the food or wine still looks the same, but now it is forbidden or worth less. The משנה separates accident (שוגג), which is exempt, from on purpose (מזיד), which must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes something ritually impure
One who mixes תרומה into regular produce, making it forbidden to non-כהנים
One who pours wine (here, as an offering to an idol)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who renders impure,
phrases.notes: He means making someone else's food טמא, which lowers its value.

phrases.english: or one who mixes in teruma, or one who pours as a libation;
unintentionally, he is exempt;
intentionally, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the steward discussion in the steps before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making food טמא, mixing in תרומה, or pouring wine to an idol: exempt by accident, liable on purpose.

steps.title: What does 'pours' mean? רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב says מנסך means really pouring the wine to an idol. שמואל says it means mixing kosher wine with forbidden idol wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated about the word 'pours': רב says it means really pouring. שמואל says it means mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two אמוראים about what the משנה means by 'מנסך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the case is a person who actually offers the other man's wine to an idol. For שמואל, the case is a person who mixes forbidden idol wine into kosher wine, so the whole mixture becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated': introduces a dispute between אמוראים

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated: 'One who pours' —
Rav says: he actually pours it as a libation;
and Shmuel says: he mixes.
phrases.notes: He mixes wine that was offered to an idol into the other man's kosher wine, so it all becomes forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word from the משנה in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: מנסך means actual pouring to an idol. שמואל: it means mixing in forbidden wine.

steps.title: Why doesn't שמואל explain it as real pouring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל refuses to read 'מנסך' in its plain meaning of actually pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it means mixing: why doesn't he say it means pouring?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about שמואל's view. This sets up the next step, which gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of מנסך is pouring, so שמואל seems to move away from the simple reading. The גמרא wants to know what pushed him to do that.

phrases.english: The one who says it means mixing,
what is the reason he did not say it means pouring?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְעָרֵב, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מְנַסֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's view in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שמואל does not accept the plain meaning of מנסך as actual pouring.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: the bigger punishment cancels the payment
steps.stepSummary: Someone who really pours wine to an idol is חייב מיתה, and because of קם ליה בדרבה מיניה he would not have to pay. So the משנה, which says he pays, cannot mean real pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: one who pours gets the bigger punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving שמואל's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of קם ליה בדרבה מיניה says that when one act deserves both death and a money payment, the person gets only the bigger punishment and does not pay. Real pouring to an idol is עבודה זרה, a death penalty act, so there would be no payment. Since the משנה says 'חייב' (he pays), שמואל explains it as mixing, which carries no death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He stands with the greater one': when one act deserves both death and payment, only the death penalty applies and he is exempt from paying
'He can tell you': introduces how a sage would defend his view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the pourer is let off easily. He faces the death penalty; he just does not also have to pay money for the same act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to the whole dispute. Step 31 shows how רב gets around it.

phrases.english: He can say to you: one who pours —
receives the greater punishment.
phrases.notes: He gets the death penalty for עבודה זרה, so he is exempt from paying for the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: מְנַסֵּךְ – קָם לֵיהּ בִּדְרַבָּה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Actual pouring carries the death penalty, so under קם ליה בדרבה מיניה there would be no payment, but the משנה says he pays.

steps.title: רב's answer: the payment starts before the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב follows רבי ירמיה: the thief owns the wine from the moment he lifts it, so he owes money then. He only becomes חייב מיתה later, when he pours. Since these happen at two different times, he still has to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one holds like רבי ירמיה, who said: he acquires the wine from the moment he lifts it; he is not liable to death until the moment he pours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב can still say the משנה means real pouring, even with the rule from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קם ליה בדרבה מיניה only works when the death penalty and the payment come at the same moment. According to רבי ירמיה, lifting the wine makes it his stolen property, so the debt starts then. The death penalty only comes later, at the pouring, so the debt was never cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the other one': the other sage in the dispute
Lifting: a way of taking ownership of an object
Liable with his life: deserving the death penalty
The act of pouring as an offering

steps.whatToRemember: רב: מנסך means real pouring. He still pays, because he owed the money from the lifting, before the death penalty came at the pouring. שמואל: real pouring would mean no payment (קם ליה בדרבה מיניה), so the משנה must mean mixing.

phrases.english: And the other one holds in accordance with Rabbi Yirmeya,
as Rabbi Yirmeya says:
from the time of lifting he acquires it;
but he is not liable to death
until the time of pouring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised by step 30 against רב's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the timing: the money debt starts at lifting, and the death penalty only at pouring.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Real pouring is one act carrying both death and payment, so קם ליה בדרבה מיניה would cancel the payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The theft (lifting) comes before the עבודה זרה (pouring), so the payment was already owed and is not cancelled.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב explain it as mixing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב, who explains מנסך as real pouring, does not accept שמואל's explanation that it means mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says it means pouring (רב), what is the reason he did not say it means mixing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question around. Before, it asked about שמואל; now it asks why רב doesn't explain the משנה the way שמואל does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw that שמואל avoided real pouring because of קם ליה בדרבה מיניה, and that רב got past that problem through רבי ירמיה. But that only shows רב *can* read it as pouring. Now the גמרא wants to know why he *must* reject the mixing reading.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says (introduces one side of a מחלוקת)
Pours wine as an offering to an idol (רב's reading)
Mixes kosher wine with forbidden idol wine (שמואל's reading)

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it means pouring,
what is the reason he did not say mixing?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְנַסֵּךְ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מְעָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 29: after asking why שמואל rejects pouring, the גמרא now asks why רב rejects mixing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רב's reason for not explaining מנסך as mixing, like שמואל?

steps.title: רב's answer begins: about mixing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts giving רב's answer, focusing on the case of mixing. The full reason continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב) could say to you: mixing…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer for רב by bringing up the case of mixing. This line is only the opening; the actual reason he rejects mixing comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אמר לך' means the גמרא is speaking on רב's behalf, explaining what he would answer. By starting with 'mixing,' it signals that it will tell us what is wrong with the mixing case as an explanation of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (the גמרא explains what a אמורא would answer)

phrases.english: He could say to you: mixing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question asked in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's answer is introduced by focusing on the mixing case; his full reason for rejecting it continues in the following text.
